log.msg: [C1] framework/core/App - WHAT IT IS: the single site-wide bootstrap object every app.js constructs once; it owns the page container and drives the boot sequence. WHAT IT DOES: config() -> render() -> await load() (imports the root Page and starts the Router) -> initialize() -> inject(), resolves an awaitable app.ready, draws a fallback error page on any boot failure. IMPLEMENTS: none of the feature list - pure bootstrap wiring, no drag/resize/card/panel/etc. IMPORTS: View, Page, Router, Font (all core siblings). README: fresh. NOTE: none.

[C1] framework/core/View - WHAT IT IS: the base DOM-wrapper class every element factory (div, p, button, ...) returns; the whole site's rendering primitive. WHAT IT DOES: wraps one DOM element, exposes chainable methods (ac/rc/classify/append/style/attr/on/html/text...), and implements the synchronous 'capturing' mechanism that lets a callback auto-append into whatever box is currently open. IMPLEMENTS: none of the feature list itself - no drag, no card, no CSS-utility classes (those live in framework.css) - it is the substrate every other module's real features are built out of. IMPORTS: nothing from ext/ux/ui. README: fresh. NOTE: this is the file every 'implements' claim elsewhere should be checked against - View gives away chainable style()/ac()/on()/toggle() etc for free, so a module that re-writes any of those is duplicating View, not adding a feature.

[C1] framework/core/Router - WHAT IT IS: turns a URL change into DOM state - intercepts link clicks, walks the Page tree to resolve a URL, and marks the active page/ancestors/links with CSS classes. WHAT IT DOES: link_clicked() filters which clicks it owns, go()/load() do the async walk and history push, activate() diffs the old and new page chains and (de)activates only the difference, mark()/mark_links() stamp .active-page/.active-ancestor/a.active/a.in-path. IMPLEMENTS: none of the feature list - routing/marking is its own thing, not drag/resize/card/tabs/etc. IMPORTS: nothing (reads only the Page/App instances handed to it, no ext/ux). README: fresh. NOTE: none.

[C1] framework/core/Page (Page.class.js + Frame.js + words.js) - WHAT IT IS: the class every page.js on the site exports - a tree node with a url, content and children, plus the 'six page words' that describe a page's own chrome (navigation/width/arrangement/surface/background/type_size) so nobody codes it by hand. WHAT IT DOES: naming()/declare()/add() build the page tree; child()/load_all_children() lazily import a page's subtree; render() draws the page (calling Frame when a word was said); columns() turns a subtree into full-height Finder-style columns; Page.Store wraps localStorage. IMPLEMENTS: resize-handle (Page.class.js:695 column_grab() - pointerdown/pointermove/lostpointercapture drags a column's width; the canonical resize handle on this site), card (Page.class.js:894 preview_card() / 903 preview_link() - the .page-preview card every 'wall' of pages uses), persistence (Page.class.js:983 Page.Store - a guarded localStorage get/set/patch/clear class with try/catch around every read/write and an in-memory fallback), tree (Page.class.js:101 declare() / 137 add() / 162 chain() - the parent/children Map every other 'tree' on the site is either this or a copy of), rail (Frame.js:132 rail() - one column of a page's children beside its content), panel (Frame.js:201 panel() - a named region opened by the arrangement word). IMPORTS: nothing from ext/ux for these five - this is the canonical implementation. README: fresh (both readme.md and generator/readme.md are current and unusually thorough). NOTE: this IS the canonical resize-handle/card/persistence implementation the parent task should measure every other module's copy against - Page.Store already absorbed one duplicate (Sidebar.Store, deleted 2026-09-18, per this task's own earlier log line), and this task's own inventory log line names a still-unlanded duplicate resize-handle at Sidebar.js:298 and layouts/shell/Shell.js:130 that should reuse column_grab() above instead.

[C1] framework/core/Page/generator - WHAT IT IS: a demo/tool that turns a random seed into a fake page tree (no filesystem, no real files) so the six page words and the columns machinery can be tried at any depth without writing a single page.js. WHAT IT DOES: gen.js draws a spec string from a seed under weighted pairing rules, tree.js turns that spec into real Page configs mounted through core's own children:, controls.js supplies the column-head menus/chips that edit the spec live, export.js can write the tree to real page.js files on disk (dev only). IMPLEMENTS: none of the feature list as its own reusable component - menu()/chips() (controls.js:55, 65) are small local select/button-group builders, not a reusable dropdown or tabs widget, and the file's own comment says they deliberately skip importing ext/Dropdown because 'core/ must not depend on ext/'. IMPORTS: nothing feature-shaped from ext/ux; gen()'s own seeded RNG (gen.js:36) is a COPY, by the file's own comment, of styles/layouts/space/draw.js's mulberry32 RNG - the file says the duplication is intentional (avoiding a core -> other-tree import), not an oversight. README: fresh - unusually thorough, explains the vocabulary, controls, exports and links every sub-tool. NOTE: none beyond the RNG copy already logged by the file itself.

[C1] framework/core/Section - WHAT IT IS: Section extends Page - a page you put inside a page, used to give one band of a page a layout (from core/Layout's catalogue) whose named boxes become mount points for children. WHAT IT DOES: render() draws a plain 2.5em box until a layout picks slots; a ResizeObserver re-decides whether the current layout still 'fits' the live box width, falling back to a plain stack below its floor; Section.Picker is the one UI control, a dropdown of approved layouts. IMPLEMENTS: none of the feature list itself as original code. IMPORTS: dropdown from ext/Dropdown (Section.js:5 import, Section.Picker extends Dropdown at Section.js:276) rather than writing its own open-list widget; core/Layout for the layout catalogue. README: fresh. NOTE: Section.js:261 'export const fits' is a second copy of core/Layout's own LayoutRule #1 with the reporting stripped off - the file's own comment (Section.js:252) says this belongs in core/Layout and was only left here because core/Layout was outside that task's write fence; a genuine unlanded duplicate for the parent's table, already self-reported.

[C1] framework/core/List - WHAT IT IS: the plain ordered array behind item.items in the Item tree - not a public API of its own, an implementation detail of Item. WHAT IT DOES: append/insert_before/remove/each/find/index_of over a plain JS array, adopting each child's .parent to the owning Item and notifying that Item's emit() on every mutation. IMPLEMENTS: none of the feature list - it is a flat ordered collection, not itself a tree, drag surface, or persistence layer (Item above it is the tree). IMPORTS: nothing. README: fresh. NOTE: none.

[C1] framework/core/Item - WHAT IT IS: the base class for any node of a persistent, nested document - the thing Panel and an editor's Block both extend - a tree with save/load, events, and a small four-key wire format. WHAT IT DOES: parent + items (a List) make it a tree; walk()/find()/contains()/move() are tree operations; on()/off()/emit() bubble events up to the root; save()/delete() delegate to the nearest ancestor holding a saver; Item.hydrate() rebuilds a tree from JSON through a type registry. IMPLEMENTS: tree (Item.js:38 root() / 39 walk() / 40 find() / 43 contains() / 32 move() - the canonical nested, reparentable tree this site's document-shaped features build on). Persistence is explicitly NOT implemented here - save()/delete() only delegate to an injected saver (e.g. FileSaver); Item itself does no I/O, by its own readme's design. IMPORTS: List (this cluster) for the ordered children; nothing else. README: fresh. NOTE: none.

[C3] framework/ext/Draggable (Draggable.js + Sortable.js) - WHAT IT IS: the site's one drag primitive - Draggable is grab-and-move for any View, Sortable extends it to reorder/reparent rows in a list. WHAT IT DOES: Draggable.js:35 grab() takes pointer capture on pointerdown and holds it for the whole gesture; drag()/release() at :46/:48 move and drop; under() at :72 hit-tests via elementsFromPoint since the dragged element still sits under the cursor. Sortable.js adds a ghost clone + placeholder (start() :12), commits a position via item.move() in release() :38, and locate()/before() (:57/:63) find the drop site by midpoint. IMPLEMENTS: drag (Draggable.js:35-79 pointer capture, hit-test, cancel; Sortable.js:12-86 ghost/placeholder/reorder - this IS the site's canonical drag implementation, everything else imports it). IMPORTS: nothing. README: fresh, thorough. NOTE: this is the module other clusters should be importing FROM, not reimplementing - worth checking every other drag-like thing found elsewhere in the audit against this file specifically.

[C3] framework/ext/grip - WHAT IT IS: the resize edge for a rail docked at a screen edge (right-side rails like ext/drawer and dev/DevBar) - a strip with a pill that rides the pointer, no permanent handle. WHAT IT DOES: grip({write, done, reset, from}) returns one View; pointerdown (:36) reads the rail's own edge once via getBoundingClientRect so a rail parked beside another rail still sizes correctly; pointermove (:50) computes px from the pointer and calls write(px); pointerup (:59) calls done(width) once; dblclick (:67) calls reset(). IMPLEMENTS: resize-handle (grip.js:27-68, the whole module is this feature, single-edge single-number case). IMPORTS: nothing beyond View. README: fresh - explicitly documents that ext/Playground used to have its own copy of this and was deleted 2026-09-06 in favor of this file, and that dev/DevBar and core/Sidebar were merged onto it 2026-09-18. NOTE: this file is NOT the same as ext/Panel/grip.js, which the owner specifically flagged as a suspicious same-name pair. They are genuinely different jobs, not a duplicate: ext/grip/grip.js drags ONE rail edge and writes a single px width (used by ext/drawer, dev/DevBar, core/Sidebar); ext/Panel/grip.js (Panel/grip.js:19-87) drags the SEAM BETWEEN TWO PANEL NEIGHBOURS and writes GROW FRACTIONS to both sides at once (:54-66), plus opens a hug/fill menu on a plain click (:73-79) and imports Draggable's registry just to read `.item` off the DOM neighbours (:48) - a job ext/grip has no concept of (it never touches two elements). Neither could stand in for the other without a rewrite. One real duplication DID surface while reading them: Panel/grip.js defines its own rAF-coalescing pointermove queue (coalesce(), Panel/grip.js:91-109) and its own comment admits it: 'Lifted from ext/demo/stage.js, never imported.' That is a second, unlanded copy of the same 10-line throttle pattern - small, but it is exactly the kind of thing the owner is asking this audit to surface, and it is a straightforward extract-to-ext/demo (or its own tiny helper) later.

[C3] framework/ext/drawer - WHAT IT IS: the site's one right-side rail - a single global dockable panel that any caller can open and fill, closed only by its own close button, that pushes the page rather than covering it. WHAT IT DOES: drawer(fn) builds the rail once (build(), :68), lets fn draw into two slots ($slot pinned head, $body scrolling body), and remembers a dragged width in one localStorage key (KEY, :18) read back on the next load (:75-76). IMPLEMENTS: none of the feature list as its own original work - it is a specific single-purpose rail widget, not a generic 'panel' system (that is ext/Panel, a different module). IMPORTS: resize-handle from ext/grip (drawer.js:2 import, used at :91) - drawer supplies only the clamp-and-remember function (size(), :59-63), the drag itself is entirely grip's. README: fresh, detailed 'Sharing it' section on the fill-don't-hold contract. NOTE: none beyond what is already in its own doc/decisions.md - this module is a clean example of correct reuse (imports the resize primitive rather than reimplementing it).

[C3] framework/ext/Dropdown - WHAT IT IS: one choice out of a list, shown as a trigger with the current picture+name and a list that opens in the browser's top layer so nothing can clip it. WHAT IT DOES: dropdown({options, value, pick}) draws a button (trigger(), :29) and a `[popover]` list (list(), :42); open()/close() use the native showPopover/hidePopover so outside-click and Escape are the browser's for free; place() (:79) positions it in viewport coordinates, flipping above the trigger if it would not fit below. IMPLEMENTS: dropdown (dropdown.js:10-113, the entire module - trigger, popover list, keyboard nav, positioning are all original here and this is the site's one implementation of the feature). IMPORTS: nothing beyond View. README: fresh. NOTE: none - only one consumer noted in its own readme (ext/Panel's properties rail), so there is nowhere else on the site duplicating this.

[C3] framework/ext/editor - WHAT IT IS: a drag-and-drop block-builder page (a demo/prototype, 'the prototype the whole thing points at' per its own Doc description), not a module other code imports. WHAT IT DOES: blocks.js defines four Item subclasses (Section/Grid/Card/Text, blocks.js:20-23) that are really just class-string + optional text, registered with Item.hydrate's type registry (blocks.js:38); page.js assembles a canvas of Sortable rows (Node class, page.js:40, extends ext/Draggable's Sortable) inside an ext/Panel workspace (page.js:243), with its own tiny undo/redo stack (History.js, snapshot-based, push-before-run at History.js:19) and property fields lifted straight from ext/layout's own vocabulary (page.js:176-182, explicitly called out in its readme as 'not a parallel vocabulary'). IMPLEMENTS: none of the feature list as ORIGINAL work - drag comes from Sortable, persistence from ext/Saver (FileSaver/LocalStorageSaver), tree from core/Item, panel/resize-handle from ext/Panel, its properties fields from ext/layout. The one genuinely original piece is History.js's undo/redo, which is not on the feature list. README: fresh, and unusually explicit that 'There is no fifth mechanism' - every region is one of the four imported systems plus this file's own glue. NOTE: this is the module the owner should point to as a positive example - it is assembled almost entirely from other ext/ modules rather than reimplementing drag, persistence, or panels; the only local invention (undo) is genuinely new work, not a duplicate of anything else in the audit so far.

[C3] framework/ext/files - WHAT IT IS: a small file browser for teaching pages - a tree of real files fetched from disk, the one you clicked, and optionally prose about it, each region a resizable/splittable panel. WHAT IT DOES: files(meta, names) lazy-loads panels.js (files.js:29-30, to keep ext/Panel's dozen modules off every page's critical path) which arranges tree/about/source as three ext/Panel leaves (panels.js:40-51); tree() (files.js:36) and nest() (files.js:72) build the folder tree from a flat path list; source() (files.js:41) uses ext/highlight if it is loaded, else a plain <pre> with a self-noted bug (a missing file's fetch does not check resp.ok, so it silently renders the SPA's index.html as if it were the file - files.js:48, already called out in its own readme). IMPLEMENTS: tree (files.js:36-85, its own nesting/grouping logic - not imported from anywhere else; core/Item's tree is a document tree, this is a plain path-grouping algorithm, a real second tree implementation but for a different job). IMPORTS: panel + resize-handle transitively via ext/Panel's workspace() (panels.js:4, imported for the split/drag/resize chrome), highlight softly (files.js:42, only if already loaded elsewhere - not a hard dependency). README: fresh. NOTE: the resp.ok gap in source()'s fallback branch is a real latent bug, not just a documentation note - it is masked today only because app.js always loads ext/highlight first, so the buggy branch never actually runs on this site.

[C3] framework/ext/highlight - WHAT IT IS: syntax highlighting bolted onto the site's `code` element factory (code.js/.css/.html/.md/.json, code.lang, code.file) using the vendored highlight.js library. WHAT IT DOES: registers five languages (highlight.js:23-27) against a hand-written accessor map (guarding against hljs's own 'c' language colliding with code.c()); patches View.prototype.html_unsafe (:219) and View.prototype.prerender (:238) so any HTML written or adopted through a View is scanned for unhighlighted <pre><code class=language-*> and highlighted synchronously, which is how markdown code fences get highlighted for free without ext/markdown needing to know about this module at all. IMPLEMENTS: none of the feature list - highlighting code is not one of the named features (closest is 'markdown', but that is ext/markdown's job; this module explicitly says its block-detection set is 'mirrors ext/markdown's block_tags on purpose... copied, not imported' at highlight.js:43-44, which is a deliberate, documented duplication of one small Set rather than an accidental one). IMPORTS: nothing beyond View and the vendored hljs. README: fresh. NOTE: the copied block_parents Set (highlight.js:45) is a real, acknowledged small duplication with ext/markdown - both files must independently agree on which tags are 'block' contexts and there is no shared source of truth for that list. Small (one line), but a future block-level tag added to one and not the other silently disagrees.

[C3] framework/ext/depth - WHAT IT IS: a page effect, not a UI primitive - turns the whole page into a 3D scene where anything wearing .depth(n) drifts on scroll and leans with the pointer, plus two sliders (Depth, Motion) to tune it live. WHAT IT DOES: depth() places two range-input sliders synchronously then wires them in a queued microtask (depth.js:57, same pattern as ext/toc per its own comment) once the page's layers actually exist; lean() (:156) tracks the pointer normalized -1..1 and writes CSS custom properties on rAF; focus() (:108) pins the parallax vanishing point to the reading line rather than the box's own centre, to avoid it running away on a long page. IMPLEMENTS: none of the feature list - it is a visual/motion effect (parallax + tilt), not a card, panel, drag surface, or any listed widget; the two <input type=range> sliders it draws are plain native inputs, not a reimplementation of anything (no card/panel/toolbar involved). IMPORTS: nothing beyond View. README: fresh. NOTE: none - this module does not overlap with anything else in this cluster or the feature list; it is a self-contained CSS-transform effect.

[C4] framework/ext/Panel (Panel.js + 19 sibling files, 5,507 lines) - WHAT IT IS: the site's general-purpose arrangeable-region system - divide any box into a tree of resizable, alignable panels, each optionally holding a live named template, with mirrors (live duplicates) and a document mode for scrolling pages. WHAT IT DOES: Panel.js (verbs only: divide/split/close/absorb/mirror/bequeath) delegates every gesture to a sibling file - PanelDrag.js extends ext/Draggable's Sortable to drag a whole panel and drop it onto an edge/centre/reorder slot (correct reuse: builds on Draggable's pointer capture rather than rewriting it); grip.js implements the seam-between-two-panels resize handle, writing GROW FRACTIONS to both neighbours on pointermove, plus its own rAF-coalescing throttle whose own comment admits it is 'Lifted from ext/demo/stage.js, never imported' (a real small unlanded duplicate, already flagged by cluster C3 reading the same file from the other side); size.js is not a gesture at all - it just turns w/h/self words into CSS classes and custom properties for fill/hug/fixed; split.js implements a SECOND, different resize handle (a per-panel edge drag that sets a FIXED length on one axis, reusing grip.js's coalesce() throttle - good internal reuse - plus its own click-to-split-here gesture with a live ghost preview); persist.js is misleadingly named - it is NOT general persistence, it is the text-edit overlay that lets a typed heading/paragraph survive a template redraw, keyed by child-index path; insert.js implements a third, independent affordance - a hover-tracked '+' that inserts a blank panel into an interior gap, with its OWN separate rAF hover-throttle (deliberately not grip.js's coalesce, per its own comment, since that one unbinds after the first click); seam.js implements a small popover-style menu (hug/fill picker) as a plain absolutely-positioned div opened by a click on the grip, rather than using ext/Dropdown's native [popover]-based implementation - a second, simpler 'popover' concept living beside the site's one Dropdown component. IMPLEMENTS: panel (the whole module IS this feature - Panel.js's verb set is the canonical arrangeable-panel system), resize-handle (grip.js + split.js, two different resize jobs, both original), drag (PanelDrag.js, but by extending ext/Draggable/Sortable rather than reimplementing pointer capture - counts as import-plus-specialization, not a fresh implementation), popover (seam.js's own hand-rolled menu - NOT ext/Dropdown's [popover] mechanism). IMPORTS: tree + persistence (Panel extends core/Item, so the tree structure, save/load and the Saver contract are all inherited, never rewritten here), drag primitives (ext/Draggable/Sortable, used by PanelDrag), dropdown (ext/Dropdown, used by properties.js's rail pickers per the readme), and per the readme's own claim, doc/controls.md's primitives are 'reused directly by ext/editor and ext/Panel' - meaning Panel also pulls small controls from ext/layout/controls.js rather than writing its own equivalents. README: fresh, unusually thorough (points to 10+ doc/ pages, lists every consumer). NOTE: the grip.js coalesce() duplicate is the one finding worth landing - it is a 10-line throttle pattern that exists in at least two places (ext/demo/stage.js and here) with no shared source; a tiny extract to ext/demo or a standalone helper would remove it. Everything else in this module is either the canonical implementation other code should copy (drag/resize/panel), or correctly built on top of another module rather than duplicating it.

[C4] framework/ext/Panel/Workspace - WHAT IT IS: the shell that HOLDS a Panel root (deliberately does not extend it, so workspace chrome never leaks into a saved document) and lets several boxes on the page mount as separate live views of that one root. WHAT IT DOES: Workspace.js's constructor loads (or seeds) the root via Item.open(store), draws a one-row top bar (add / fill-vs-document toggle / document name / viewport slot) in draw_bar(), and mount() can be called again to add a second, third... view of the same root (N viewports, one document); documents.js is the file-backed persistence scheme - one Saver per named document under /data/panels/<name>.json plus a hand-maintained /data/panels/index.json list, switching to LocalStorageSaver automatically off localhost. IMPLEMENTS: toolbar (Workspace.js:143 draw_bar() - its own small button row, original code, not imported from anywhere else on the site). IMPORTS: persistence mechanism (ext/Saver's FileSaver/LocalStorageSaver do the actual read/write I/O; documents.js only adds the naming/indexing scheme on top - the mechanism is imported, the file-layout convention is this module's own and is a reasonable, undangerous kind of 'implements' since there is nothing else on the site doing multi-document file storage to copy from), tree (Panel/Item, as in the parent cluster), panel + resize-handle (transitively, since the root it holds is a Panel). README: fresh. NOTE: none - this is a thin, well-scoped shell; nothing here duplicates code that exists elsewhere.

[C4] framework/ext/layout - WHAT IT IS: a toolbar-plus-drawer pair you drop over any box, a bare element, or a live Page, that makes its container words (flex/grid/gap/pad) and, for a selected child, its CSS provenance editable live - built for demo and guide pages that want to let the reader poke at a layout, not for shipping UI. WHAT IT DOES: layout.js draws layout.bar() (a small original toolbar of word-controls plus a 'tune' button) and region() (hover-to-highlight, click-to-select any flex/grid child, one level deep); panel.js owns the selection state and opens ext/drawer's rail to show it, wiring Escape/outside-click/popstate to deselect; body.js renders the selection's live CSS rules by reading ext/CSSDoc's cssdoc.rules() (the CSSOM, not a guess) and groups them by owning file/layer; controls.js supplies four small primitives (pick/menu/toggle/knob) that, per this module's own readme, are 'reused directly by ext/editor and ext/Panel' rather than each writing their own. IMPLEMENTS: toolbar (layout.js:27 layout.bar() - an original small toolbar, a second, independent toolbar implementation alongside ext/Panel's controls.css/properties.js rail and Workspace's draw_bar() - three different toolbar-shaped things on the site, though each serves a genuinely different surface so this reads as parallel evolution rather than one being a copy of another), css-utility (arguably none directly - body.js READS the cascade via ext/CSSDoc rather than restating utility classes). IMPORTS: resize-handle + rail (ext/drawer, used for the whole sliding properties rail - panel.js:2 import), popover-adjacent picker (none new - controls.js's menu() is a plain native <select>, not a custom dropdown, so it does not duplicate ext/Dropdown), CSS provenance reading (ext/CSSDoc, body.js:4). Not one readme was found STALE - every readme that existed still matched its code.

FINDING 2 - the card. The owner suspected UI cards, and they were right. I counted every CSS rule on the site that declares a card SHAPE of its own - a selector whose block sets its own background, its own padding AND its own border or radius. There are 27 of them, in 22 files. The framework already has the answer: framework.css gives you the same shape as four utility words on a plain div, `surface pad flex v gap`, with no rules at all, and core/Page's own preview_card() is the one real card COMPONENT (144 call sites). The 27 are spread as: 11 under imagine/, 5 under layouts/, 2 in dev/DevBar, 2 in ui/background, 1 in styles/stacks, 1 in websites, and 5 in realms outside this audit's scope. On top of the CSS the minions found the same shape rebuilt in JS four more times independently: ext/DesignTool has THREE separate 4-line cards() helpers (library/patterns.js:21, library/bad/traps.js:19, tests/cases.js:24), and websites/Site.js:419 has its own static card() while layouts/browse next door correctly reuses core's preview(). Four imagine/ pages (game, team, youtube/panel, and the review page) each hand-built the same three-column card the owner asked for, with no shared component between them.

FINDING 3 - the answer to the owner's actual question is better than expected, and the reason matters. The features the owner named by name have ALREADY been consolidated, and the site's own readmes record the day each merge landed. Resize handles: ext/grip is now the one implementation, and core/Sidebar, layouts/shell/Shell.js, ext/drawer and dev/DevBar all import it - the 2026-09-18 study called Shell.grab() a byte-for-byte rewrite of Sidebar.grab() and a minion re-checked both files today: each is now five lines passing callbacks into the shared grip(). Drag and drop: ext/Draggable/Sortable is the one implementation; ext/Panel/PanelDrag and ux/Tree/Tree.Drag both extend it rather than copy it, and Make's own drag model was lifted INTO ux/Tree on 2026-09-17 so the site would have one. Persistence: core/Page.Store is the one localStorage guard and ext/Saver's LocalStorageSaver now delegates to it. Trees: ux/Tree won, and its own compare page documents the three implementations that lost. So the honest headline is that the live framework has very little ACCIDENTAL duplication left - what remains is concentrated in two places, and neither is a component.

FINDING 4 - the duplicates that are real but deliberately kept, so a reader does not mistake them for oversights. Three mechanisms exist for a list of choices that opens near a trigger: ux/Menu (a native <details>, no JS positioning), ext/Dropdown (native [popover], top layer, JS-positioned, shows a current value) and ux/Popover's own menu() helper (also [popover], with arrow-key nav). Each serves a slightly different case and none of the three readmes names the other two. Two hover-tooltips: ui/tooltip is CSS only, ux/Popover's tooltip() is JS in the top layer - the same job twice, undocumented as a pair. Four snapshot-plus-append-log persistence contracts, all built on ext/JSONL's transport but sharing no class: imagine/importance, imagine/stream, imagine/cms/json and imagine/paging/make/made.js. Three toolbars with no shared code: ext/layout's bar(), ext/Panel/Workspace's draw_bar() and dev/DevBar's tab strip. And the mulberry32 random-number function is copied into four files (core/Page/generator/gen.js, styles/layouts/space/draw.js, layouts/labs/trees/gen.js, ui/background's scatter) - five lines each, each copy deliberate and commented, because sharing it would cross a tree boundary the framework does not want crossed.

Exactly one of everything found meets that bar: core/Section/Section.js:261 exports a fits() that its OWN comment calls a copy of core/Layout/rules.js's first rule with the reporting taken off, left behind only because core/Layout was outside that task's write fence.
